section_1.title: The Intuition: Why some guesses are 'better'
section_1.content: Introduce the goal of Wordle as a search problem. Explain that a 'good' guess isn't just about matching letters, but about narrowing down the search space as quickly as possible.
section_1.example: If you guess 'ARISE' and eliminate half the remaining dictionary, you've gained more 'information' than if you guess 'XYLYL' and eliminate almost nothing.

section_2.title: Defining Information: The 'Surprise' Factor
section_2.content: Define information content (Self-Information) as the negative log probability: I(x) = -log2(P(x)). Explain that rare events provide more information than common ones.
section_2.example: Visual: A scale showing an 'Improbable Event' (a coin landing on its edge) creating a large spike in information versus a 'Common Event' (a coin landing on heads) creating a small flat line.

section_3.title: Calculating Entropy: The Expected Information Gain
section_3.content: Introduce Shannon Entropy as the average information (uncertainty) of a guess: H(X) = Σ p(x) log2(1/p(x)). A guess with high entropy splits the remaining word list into equal-sized buckets.
section_3.example: Visual: A 'Bucket Analogy'. The word 'CRANE' acts as a sorting machine, distributing 2,300 words into various colored buckets based on the green/yellow/gray pattern result.

section_4.title: The Strategy: Maximizing Entropy
section_4.content: Show how an algorithm chooses a word not by looking for the secret word, but by looking for the word that produces the most 'informative' distribution of outcomes.
section_4.example: An 'AI Detective' bot (modeled as a robotic fox) calculates entropy for every possible guess, selecting the one that 'tames' the uncertainty of the dictionary the fastest.

section_5.title: Wrap-up: From Wordle to Reality
section_5.content: Summarize how Information Theory principles apply to fields beyond games, such as medical diagnostics, data compression, and signal processing.
section_5.example: Just as a detective eliminates suspects in a mystery, medical diagnostic trees use entropy to determine which test reduces the 'uncertainty' of a patient's condition most efficiently.

section_1.title: The Intuition: Why some guesses are 'better'
lecture_lines: Wordle is a search problem for secret words.
A great guess narrows search space quickly.
Information gain measures how much we learn.
animations: Fade in a 'Wordle' grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wordle.svg] at #FFFFFF with title 'The Intuition'. Wait 4s.

section_2.title: Defining Information: The 'Surprise' Factor
lecture_lines: Rare outcomes surprise us, providing more information.
Information is the negative log of probability.
Frequent events carry very little surprise value.
animations: Show 'Event X' icon in #00FFFF, label it 'Event'. Wait 4s.
Morph 'Event X' into 'Information Content' formula: I(x) = -log2(P(x)) in #FFFFFF with 'I(x)', 'log2', and 'P(x)' color-labeled. Wait 4s.
Scale 'I(x)' formula up and highlight the negative coefficient to emphasize surprise. Wait 4s.

section_3.title: Calculating Entropy: The Expected Information Gain
lecture_lines: Entropy calculates the average information in guesses.
Guessing splits possibilities into equal-sized buckets.
High entropy choices resolve uncertainty fastest.
We average information gain across all outcomes.
Formula sums probability times surprise for all.
animations: Display 'Probability Distribution' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/histogram.svg] histogram in #FF00FF, labeling x-axis outcomes. Wait 4s.
Overlay 'Entropy' summation formula: H(X) = Σ P(x)I(x) in #FFFFFF, labeling 'P(x)' and 'I(x)' components. Wait 4s.
Animate sequence: iterate through histogram bars, flashing each bar while adding its P(x)I(x) contribution to the H(X) sum. Wait 4s.
Place a green [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/target.svg] target icon as a 'Goal Anchor' at the computed final H(X) coordinate. Wait 4s.
Pulse the 'Goal Anchor' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/target.svg] target icon to highlight reaching maximum information gain. Wait 4s.

section_4.title: The Strategy: Maximizing Entropy
lecture_lines: Algorithms don't search for the secret word.
They prioritize the most informative guess instead.
The bot tames uncertainty using entropy metrics.
Every outcome distribution is analyzed for gain.
Entropy maximization is the key strategy here.
